question.text: Mr. Vikram Bhatia is a Lead Investor raising a Syndicate of INR 40 crore for a Pre-Series A in 'Zephyr Robotics'. He commits INR 8 crore himself and raises INR 32 crore from co-investors at a 20% carry. Exit at INR 120 crore after 3 years. Per the workbook's syndicate carry example (syndicate investors, including the lead investor, pay carry on the profit amount to the lead investor), how much carry does Mr. Vikram receive?

answer.text: INR 24 crore — 20% of the gross exit proceeds.
INR 16 crore — 20% of the total profit (120 − 40 = 80), in line with the workbook example.
INR 12.8 crore — carry only on the co-investors' portion of profit, excluding the lead's own contribution.
INR 8 crore — carry equals the lead's own committed capital.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's syndicate example specifies that syndicate investors, including the lead investor, pay carry on the profit amount to the lead investor. Total exit = INR 120 crore; total investment = INR 40 crore; profit = INR 80 crore; carry at 20% on the profit = INR 16 crore. The Trap: "INR 24 crore" applies carry to gross exit instead of profit, contrary to the workbook. "INR 12.8 crore" excludes the lead's own contribution from the carry base, which the workbook example does not do. "INR 8 crore" has no formula basis in the source. Note: The syndicate carry example appears on page 208; the workbook does not specify a separate hurdle, catch-up or no-self-carry treatment for syndicates.
